header.capture_method: set -a; . ~/.factory-dispatcher/env; set +a; venv/bin/python with sys.path += apps/factory-dispatcher; substrate.default_store(); GET only (httpx.request wrapped to refuse any non-GET); every population paged by offset at limit 200 until a short page (dev.task, dev.note per parent_id, arch.release, arch.change, arch.requirement_conformance, dev.release, arch.observation); links via GET /beads/{id}/links (unpaged route).
header.date_in_filename: The filename keeps the 2026-09-23 date the design (docs/plans/2026-09-23-design-r2612-steerable-and-legible.md, 'Fixtures the outer loop commits with the first specs (D7)') and the PC-* acceptance criteria name; the capture itself is dated by captured_at.
header.changed_since_design: The design names charters R26.09, R26.11 and R26.10. R26.12 (#1014's predecessor charter PR) and R26.13 (#1014) have since been chartered and their arch.release beads exist in state planned, so the open set at this capture is R26.09, R26.10, R26.11, R26.12, R26.13; all five charters are included verbatim and every per_release block covers all five. The design's 2026-09-23 figures (R26.09 rework ~44%, R26.11 ~14%, R26.11 blocking 81.8%) were measured two days earlier; this header's numbers supersede them for the fixture.
header.release_states_note: release_states covers every arch.release bead, open or not
header.policy_note: The design's proposed first values (for_grant #5; decision P4 of the sprints-55-57 plan ratifies urgency_bands/aging_days only). health-policy.json is B0b and is NOT committed here. If the Operator sets different values the expected_* fields below must be recomputed; the raw per_release counts do not change.

definitions.bound: dev.task beads with an incoming delivers edge on the release bead (any task state, superseded included)
definitions.superseded: bound tasks in state superseded (reported beside bound; neither removed from bound nor added to the union)
definitions.request_changes_tasks: bound tasks with >=1 review note verdict == 'request-changes'
definitions.requeued_tasks: bound tasks with >=1 status note with resets_attempts truthy AND non-null requeue_reason
definitions.union_tasks: request_changes_tasks | requeued_tasks (task-level; a task counts once)
definitions.rate: union_tasks / bound, as a fraction; null when bound < min_classified (rate_raw keeps the unsuppressed value)
definitions.rate_excluding_superseded: the alternative reading (superseded removed from bound and union) -- recorded so a B12 author choosing it can check; expected_rework_fires is the SAME under both readings at this capture
definitions.open_bound_to_other_releases: open tasks (state not in done/archived/superseded, release-status TERMINAL_TASK_STATES) whose delivers edge names a release other than this one
definitions.true_unbound: open tasks with no delivers edge and no release_ref_waived (compute_unassigned's 'neither'; the same for every release)
definitions.balance: release-status build_release_report's class counts (bound tasks whose outcome_ref names a charter outcome, class from the outcome's work_class, superseded included); actual_pct null when classified < min_classified (B1's n<5 rule) or the class is declared > 0 with nothing classified (ABSENT)
definitions.expected_rework_fires: rate is not null and rate*100 >= policy.rework_rate_pct
definitions.expected_class_over_share: classes with actual_pct not null and actual_pct > declared_pct + balance_tolerance_pct (tolerance read as percentage POINTS)
definitions.expected_class_over_share_relative: the other reading of the tolerance (actual_pct > declared_pct * (1 + tolerance/100)); recorded because the design does not say which; B12's author states which it implements
definitions.expected_class_absent_at_midpoint: at now = captured_at + 22 days: classes declared > 0 with actual_count 0, when elapsed_pct(now) >= absent_after_elapsed_pct; elapsed_pct = (now - opened_at)/(target_at - opened_at) in days

header.queue_order_file: null by design: no queue-order file exists before B8; AC-9 reads 'unknown'
header.note_reduction: Each note is {id, created_at, created_by, content: {kind, body_first_line = dispatch.redact_sensitive_output(body).splitlines()[0][:200], ...kind extras}}. status: + environmental_fault_signature, resets_attempts, preserved_choice, releases_work, expedite, class_of_service, expedite_reason, expedite_until (each only if present on the stored note) and requeue_reason (derived: for a resets_attempts note the text after guards._REQUEUE_REASON_MARKER 'Reason:' with the _REQUEUE_PRESERVED_SUFFIX_MARKER tail stripped, parsed from the FULL redacted body; else null). review: + verdict, url (+ pr_url when the stored note carries one). question: + blocking, answers_ref. answer: + answers_ref (+ releases_work when present -- guards.open_questions reads it on the answer, so it is kept there too). attachment: + url. Dropped: provenance, context, trust_tier, full bodies. To feed a reduced note to a guards/dispatch function that reads content.body, map body_first_line -> body; every prefix those functions test for is on the first line (verified at build: see header.reconstruction_check).
header.redaction: no provenance, no worker/model fields, no full bodies; PR URLs kept
header.no_count_in_ac: PC-ASR-008 AC-7/AC-9 and PC-DEL-003 AC-1 assert against these header fields; no count is written into an AC.

R26.09.name: Productive from the console; the graph answers what breaks
R26.09.objective:
The factory gains an operator surface that is a capability rather than a terminal. RE-AIMED 2026-09-20 by the Operator: that surface is the CONSOLE, not a phone client. He now reaches the workstation directly from Claude Code on his phone, which satisfies reading and acting on the board without a gateway client at all, and he asked for the board he actually uses to be built out instead. So the outcomes below keep the objective and change the surface: the board answers where a release stands and whether the factory is running, and an operator can stop the factory from it. What survives from the original framing is the part that was never about the phone — the graph answering what a change affects, the technology layer, the risk register — and the discipline that a capability claim carries a dated probe rather than a demo. TWO THINGS THE RE-AIM DROPPED FROM THE ORIGINAL PARAGRAPH AND SHOULD NOT HAVE, restored here 2026-09-20 after the gate found them: this arc is the first chartered under the 2026-09-12 north-star record (docs/plans/2026-09-12-decision-record-north-star-itsm-sdlc-ea-on-beads.md), an ITSM/SDLC/EA platform on beads with Temporal underneath, with the EA model as the primary signal for what the Product Owner puts into the factory next; and the declared balance below is chosen to correct the skew the R26.05/R26.06 balance reports are showing, not to mirror it. Neither had anything to do with the phone, and declared_balance is unchanged, so deleting its rationale while keeping its numbers left the numbers unexplained.

RE-DATED 2026-09-19 (decision record docs/plans/2026-09-19-decision-record-audit-against-the-north-star.md, Release Manager reconciliation): target_at moves from 2026-12-06 to 2026-10-05, the end of sprint 54, in which the remaining feature beads (S52-1, S52-2, S52-4, S53-1) file first and keep dispatch priority over R26.11; outcomes still not delivered then close with a written decision.

outcomes.statement: RETIRED 2026-09-20 by the Operator, undelivered and not to be built. It read: from the Claude phone app you can see the board, read a bead with its notes and links, and read the gate verdict on its PR, through the gateway's scope-gated bead capability. He now runs Claude Code on his phone against the workstation, which reads all of that directly and needs no gateway client, so the outcome is satisfied by a different route and the work is cancelled rather than deferred. NO PHONE CLIENT WAS BUILT, BUT THE OUTCOME IS NOT EMPTY, and an earlier draft of this sentence said it was. Measured 2026-09-20: one bead is bound to O-1 through a delivers edge and it is done -- 3b8ae415, merged as #814 on 2026-09-13, which froze the substrate's fourteen-route REST surface that six module families consume. That is enabling work the retirement does not waste: the contract it pinned is under the console's own proxy as much as under any gateway client. What was cancelled is the phone-facing capability, which was never started. The console board he does use is served by the console's own proxy, not by this capability, and is carried by O-9.

PARTLY DELIVERED, REMAINDER RETIRED 2026-09-20 by the Operator. The retired half read: from the phone you can answer a blocking question, add a note, requeue with a reason, supersede a spec. Claude Code on the phone does all of it directly, so no phone client is needed. THE WORK IS NOT CANCELLED, THOUGH, AND AN EARLIER DRAFT SAID IT WAS: most of the act half was already built gateway-side, and the console is its consumer. Measured 2026-09-20, six beads carry a delivers edge to O-2 and five are done -- 625c4d12 moved the task-intake contract to the intake's own owner, a86f0ccf collapsed eight bead-store clients to one, 5184eba3 made filing a capability on the gateway that refuses exactly what the CLI refuses, da959d13 routed the console through that capability instead of writing dev.* beads straight to the substrate, and ccfe0a3b closed the note half of the same intake. What is cancelled is the phone as the caller. The capability underneath it is shipped and in use. DELIVERED: merge-by-verdict exists as a capability that executes only a MERGE written by a fresh-context gate and refuses everything else, shipped dark in PR #969 on 2026-09-20 — granted to no client, behind a second disabled flag, with the conditions of any future grant written in that PR body: merge order is a human precondition, no decision record grants it yet, and two defects must close first (a verdict is self-certifiable by the PR's own author, and nothing refuses a protected path). Its motivation was largely the phone, so the grant may never be sought; dark and unused costs nothing and the reasoning is recorded.

The technology layer exists: the observer lands arch.ci from the cluster it can reach and records a dated cannot-evaluate outcome when it cannot, and application.depends_on is resolved to a known set or an assessed none — the 26 unknown of 2026-09-12 becomes a number that the nightly coverage report carries as a trend.

The graph answers what a change affects: change → application → CI → service over typed edges, served as one capability on the gateway and one console view, with the coverage the answer was computed on declared beside it — and an unassessed application reads as unknown, never as unaffected.

A risk register exists on beads: arch.risk leaves reserved with a content model, a registered state machine and admitted edges, and the risks this platform already accepts in prose — the single-node SPOF, the mutable :latest deploy path, the single-host factory — are filed with an owner and a review date rather than carried in an amendment's rationale.

RE-AIMED 2026-09-20 from the phone to the console, and more load-bearing than before, not less: a console that can ACT on the factory must not widen who can reach it. Every factory capability call is attributable to a named client and the scope it used; read, write and merge are separate grants -- the three scopes that exist, measured 2026-09-20: factory.read, factory.write and factory.merge appear in the tree and factory.control appears nowhere, so a control scope is this outcome's open question and not one of its facts; and that is established by a check against the gateway's own audit shape rather than by inspection. The re-aim is why this stays: O-10 adds a control that stops the factory from a browser, and dev.finding 3e8e8a5b records that a previous 'granted to no client' claim was true of service tokens and false of human identities because of a wildcard rewrite in application code. What a human in the console actually holds is therefore a question this outcome owes an answer to before O-10's control ships.

RE-AIMED 2026-09-20. It read: the phone path is proven by a dated probe, not a demo. The phone path is retired, but the discipline is the reason this outcome existed and it now attaches to the surface being built: the console operator surface is proven by a dated probe rather than a demo — a check that reads what O-9 and O-10 claim to show and compares it against the store and the schedule, run each release cycle so the claim carries a date. the Operator reaching the board from his phone on 2026-09-20 is a demonstration in exactly the sense this outcome was written to distrust, and it is recorded as such rather than as evidence.

Operational work the factory absorbs during this arc — the defects a running system produces — lands here rather than going unaccounted, and is held to the declared share at sprint planning rather than allowed to crowd out the outcomes above.

The board answers where every open release stands. For each release that is not yet closed you can see it at a glance: which outcomes are delivered, which are in progress, and which are still only declared — read from the releases and the beads bound to them rather than from a hand-maintained list, so it cannot drift from what the factory actually did. Asked for by the Operator on 2026-09-20: he uses the board for progress and wants the release picture on it.

The board says whether the factory is running, and lets an operator stop it. Its operational state is visible without a terminal — whether dispatch is paused and why, whether the worker is alive and at which revision, what is queued, running and held, and when the last tick did something — and a control on that surface pauses the factory, recording who paused it and why. Asked for by the Operator on 2026-09-20. The control is a write from a browser to a schedule, so it lands only on the terms O-6 sets.

R26.10.name: The deploy path becomes reversible
R26.10.objective:
Everything this platform ships runs behind a tag that moves. Measured 2026-09-18 over infrastructure/k8s/: ten `:latest` image references against one `@sha256:` reference, eight of the ten first-party and those eight carrying `pullPolicy: Never`. So what is running in production cannot be named, a red build still poisons a node, and a rollback has no immutable prior version to return to. PC-DEL-001/AC-1, PC-DEL-001/AC-2 and PC-TRU-001/AC-1 have stood at `fail` since 2026-08-29.

THE BLOCKER IS A CREDENTIAL, NOT A PERMISSION, AND NAMING IT IS THE POINT OF THIS CHARTER. An earlier draft of this objective said the work defers because its paths are closed to the factory. That is false and the repository disproves it: the task-intake contract forbids only `.github/workflows/**`, and the factory has already been dispatched against `infrastructure/k8s/` for this very outcome — dev.task 7fafb95f (PR #476) landed the digest mechanism and is `done`. PC-DEL-001/AC-1 records the real cause: `gh variable list` and `gh api .../actions/variables` both return empty, so ZOT_REGISTRY and ZOT_PUSH_ENABLED do not exist and nothing publishes. In its own words, 'G1a is the whole remaining blocker'. AC-2 is downstream of it — nothing can be pinned to a digest that was never pushed.

G1a has not moved since 2026-07-29 and has led three consecutive sprint plans without moving. It is a credential act reserved to the Operator, with a written procedure at docs/runbooks/g1a-registry-push.md. It is the ENTRY PRECONDITION FOR O-1 AND O-2: until the registry accepts a push, those two are unreachable and scheduling them is theatre. O-3 and O-4 are NOT gated on it — O-3 is a console read-path with no relationship to the registry, and O-4 is absorption. They are named here because an earlier draft of this paragraph said 'every outcome below', which is false for both and would defer the Amendment 35 outcome behind a credential act for the second time, on the same shape of wrong premise this charter was rewritten to remove. That is why the work carried from R26.01 to R26.02 and now here — not neglect, and not a path permission.

It carries one further outcome for a related reason: the console read-path that R26.06 could not execute. That gates the Amendment 35 store decision, and a path decided on paper that has never served a browser is the failure the analysis was commissioned to prevent.

It closes when a deploy can be named, and undone, with a number against how long undoing took.

RE-SEQUENCED 2026-09-19 (decision record docs/plans/2026-09-19-decision-record-audit-against-the-north-star.md, D11): sprints 54-56 are taken by R26.11 'The tree says what the platform is'; this charter moves to 57-59. Digest-pinned images and a one-command rollback are cheaper once R26.11 has retired the finance-reporting deployment, the dev tier and the parking automation, so the order is deliberate rather than a delay.

Operational work the factory absorbs during this arc — the defects a running system produces — lands here rather than going unaccounted, and is held to the declared share at sprint planning rather than allowed to crowd out the outcomes above. R26.11.name: The tree says what the platform is
R26.11.objective: The 2026-09-19 audit against the north star (docs/audits/2026-09-19-audit-against-the-north-star.md) measured a platform whose binding document, tree, store and cluster each still carry the shape of decisions the platform has since reversed: retired technology that runs in every CI pass, ratified amendments whose executable clauses nobody filed, household workloads inside the product's gateway and namespaces, four bead namespaces the architecture never sanctioned, nightly reconcilers that mint observations nothing resolves, and test suites that pin behaviour the platform decided not to have. This arc removes what does not tie back to Amendment 39 — an ITSM/SDLC/EA platform on beads with Temporal underneath, finance a vertical — in Tidy-First order: delete before refactor, freeze contracts before moving anything, tests last so that code deletions take their tests with them. It is deliberately weighted to enabling, blocking and security work and declares no feature outcome: the feature this release delivers is a tree, a store and a document that describe the same platform. Its two amendment-class moves (the finance workflow runtime out of the gateway; the EA/ITSM reconcilers out of the SDLC dispatcher into an in-cluster host) are named as the arc after, not folded in. Chartered on the 2026-09-19 decision record; R26.10 moves from sprints 54-56 to 57-59 because digest-pinned images are cheaper once the workloads this arc retires are gone. It opens on 2026-09-22 with the close of R26.05 the same day (the standing rule of three), takes over absorption from R26.05/O-9 on that date, and runs beside R26.09's final sprint, whose remaining feature work keeps dispatch priority. The publication outcomes R26.05 carries are re-issued as their own charter when a slot opens, sequenced after R26.10: clean, then reversible, then publish.

outcomes.statement: Retired technology and residue are gone from the tree, the suite and the host: the bd/Dolt adapter and its Gastown projector, the codex worker entry, the Gemini gate cost scripts, the Goose fixtures, the Qdrant search path and the prod-disabled bead cache, the Vikunja secrets, the iTop-era compliance beads, the never-run gate scripts and spikes, the never-demonstrated knowledge engine and vision path, the finance workflows that structurally cannot produce output, and the merged-residue branches, worktrees and custom refs — and a repository check refuses a retired name's return outside the archive and the amendment ledger.

The binding document, the bead-object inventory and the EA model describe the Amendment 39 platform: the target diagram, pillars, layout, roadmap and decisions table no longer name Goose, Gas City, Vikunja, a vector store or verticals that were never built; the inventory lists every namespace the store holds and the registry validates each; and a document that describes the running system carries the date it was measured and an owner, or lives in the archive — enforced by a checker in the readme-conformance pattern rather than by an editing rule.

The household is separated from the product: the parking automation that never paid once is retired by amendment, the dev tier that nothing promotes through is retired, the one-page finance-reporting deployment is folded or deleted, the outstanding Terraform apply that revokes the retired Goose identity and the Vikunja records has run, and the finance vertical is reduced to the workflows a person reads — so what remains on the cluster and in the gateway is either the product or a declared operator estate, never both under one credential.

When a reconciler or a scheduled workflow fails, someone is told: every registered schedule's most recent run is a measured fact with an alert behind it, the EA reconciler that failed every tick for three days is fixed at the paging defect that caused it, the writers that have 422'd silently since August conform to the store's provenance contract, and the nightly reporters update standing observations instead of minting dated ones nobody resolves.

The test suites are measured and rationalised: a coverage baseline exists and cannot drop unnoticed, the dispatcher's 7,600-line test monolith is split by the module it pins, the twenty-six test names duplicated across files are merged on assertion-identity evidence rather than by name, tests that pinned retired technology leave with it, the one state-mutating finance module gains tests, hand-rolled store doubles across every tree sit under the ratchet, and each requirement criterion that claims a test names one that resolves.

Access narrows to what was decided: an authenticated household member holds the scopes granted to them rather than every scope, a granted-but-unchecked scope is revoked rather than carried, the identity that writes a bead is drawn from a declared vocabulary the store validates forward-only, and Terraform drift between the edge configuration and the provider is measured on a schedule rather than discovered by audit.

Operational work the factory absorbs during this arc — the defects a running system produces — lands here rather than going unaccounted, and is held to the declared share at sprint planning rather than allowed to crowd out the outcomes above. From 2026-09-22 this outcome, not R26.05/O-9, is where absorption binds; R26.09/O-8 takes only defects in R26.09's own deliverables.

R26.12.name: The queue has an order and the release has a pulse
R26.12.objective: Measured 2026-09-23 (main a32031fa; re-read at 9b0307c6 2026-09-23T18:45Z): the factory picks the oldest pending bead and nothing else (dispatch.py:4021), so R26.11's 'keeps dispatch priority' sentence has no carrier and the Operator's own board control sat last in FIFO until forced by hand; four status surfaces say 'claimable' from a predicate only the dispatcher completes with its breaker; that breaker cannot let go once latched — beads are fenced today on two signatures, most on one undiagnosed heartbeat-timeout signature (latched fixture header) — and a bead whose premise is missing from main is dispatched anyway; release health is computed nightly into dated observations nobody reads while R26.11 stands at blocking 81.8% against 10% declared; the release report mis-applies its waiver filter and cannot say UNMEASURED; and the graph cannot say what a release did to the portfolio because the edge writer resolves through a field the dispatcher never sets. This arc builds three things from facts the platform already records, aligned to an ITSM/SDLC/EA platform on beads (Amendment 39). The queue gains one selector every surface reads and a declared order — nearest in_flight time box first, predecessors before dependents, oldest first with bounded aging, one budgeted expiring emergency an operator sets with a reason and attests with a note, same store + same clock + same policy revision giving the same order — with every position explained on the board, in the claim note and in the worker's prompt, the breaker releasing on the success and requeue notes it already ignores, and one idle reason saying why nothing is running: complete on the CLI, on the board with host-only facts named as not served rather than shown healthy. Release health becomes a governed record per open release: state machine, policy document under the loader, alerts that transition and dedupe without falling silent, task-level rework and gate coverage as signals, close readiness, unknown rendered as unknown, a disposition that moves state — after the two remaining release-number defects are fixed. And the release reaches the changes it made, the applications they touched and the verdicts that admitted them by typed edges. It declares no paging. It opens 2026-10-06 with R26.09's close the day before (rule of three) and runs beside R26.11's sprints 55-56 and R26.10's 57; under its own rule R26.11 outranks it in sprint 55 in principle, though every R26.11 bead pending at this write is held. The arc after: the precedes edge, refusing closing->released on readiness (293af9d3), regresses edges via R26.11's filer, the event-log claimable time once 72067fdb lands, host facts on the board once a store carrier exists, the reconciler host move R26.11 reserves. Outcome retirement as a validated field joins by the Operator's charter PR if he admits the field (for_grant #6).

outcomes.statement: There is one selector. Every surface that says a bead is claimable, runnable or next — the dispatcher's pick, its claim-time re-check, the CLI status, the board's badge, the queue endpoint — reads the same function with the same gates, so a green count means the next tick would claim something and a latched bead reads latched everywhere; a caller ratchet in Python and TypeScript refuses a second implementation; and an order that cannot be computed reads unknown rather than re-sorted.

The queue runs in a declared order and you can see why. Among in_flight releases, work for the one whose target date is nearest goes first; a predecessor never sits behind the work waiting on it; nothing starves past a bounded age; and the same store at the same clock under the same policy revision gives the same order on every host — the served order and the CLI order each name the policy revision they computed with, and the gate compares them, because the worker checkout and the hub image can hold different revisions of docs/releases/policy/health-policy.json and this arc makes that visible, not impossible — with each bead's position, priority, inherited tier, age and every hold reason on the board, in its claim note and in the worker's prompt. Charter dates already recorded are the only between-release input; if R26.09 is still in_flight when this lands, its work goes first by that rule and no charter is edited. The age a bead has waited is read from the bead event log -- when it last entered pending -- the source R26.11 landed as #992 on 2026-09-23.

the Operator can put one thing first. An operator verb marks at most one bead emergency with a reason and an expiry and attests it with a note that carries the operator's provenance; a second is refused; the marker does not survive a requeue, and a superseded bead is terminal so its marker is never read; and the PR that lands it carries the 'Emergency change: true' line the merge path already reads, so the change record counts it in the vocabulary arch.change already has.

The release numbers the Product Owner reads are right before anything alerts on them: the waiver filter is applied to both populations, the notes distinguish UNMEASURED from NOT DELIVERED, and a balance below five classified tasks is a count, never a percentage. Lands first, because health inherits whatever the report gets wrong. (The --release scoping defect is already fixed on main by #855 and is pinned, not rebuilt.)

Release health is a managed record, not a report. Each open release has one arch.release_health bead measuring against it, with a registered state machine, content the store validates, thresholds in docs/releases/policy/health-policy.json under the loader and refused at intake to every lane, an hourly reconciler that writes nothing when nothing changed, task-level rework and gate coverage among its signals, a close-readiness reading the close runbook consults, unknown rendered with the failed input named and never as zero or on_track, alerts that post on a transition, stay quiet while unchanged, re-announce weekly and escalate a persistent unknown — none opening an incident — and a disposition the outer loop records that moves the record to accepted until a date or a change. The record ships beside the dated observations, which stop only when the Operator re-scopes R26.11/O-4's clause.

The release picture and the dispatch reasoning are on the board the Operator uses and in the manifest the gate reads: each open release shows its health state, fired signals, per-outcome delivery, close readiness, disposition and how old the measurement is; the pending column is in the order the factory will take it, fetched once, with a held section and one idle-reason panel that says why nothing is running from the inputs the in-cluster hub can read (paused and why, in-flight, the queue) and names the three it cannot (worker revision, base ref, tunnel keeper) as not served on this host rather than showing them healthy; and the gate's manifest carries release, outcome, predecessors, class of service and prior verdicts so merge order is stated from declared facts. THE BOARD HALF OF THIS OUTCOME IS CONDITIONAL: every release-picture surface the console reads runs through the hub's factory_status loader, whose FACTORY_STATUS_REPO_ROOT is unset in production by a recorded decision (OPS-110 arm (c)); it answers not_configured until that decision is reversed, which is the Operator's (for_grant #8). Until then the CLI and the gate's manifest carry the release picture, and the queue endpoint -- loaded through FACTORY_DISPATCHER_ROOT as #993's schedule route is -- carries the dispatch reasoning.

The factory cannot stop silently. A bead the environmental-fault breaker has fenced is released by the success or requeue note the record already holds, with nothing erased; a bead whose premise is absent from main is returned without spending an attempt and latches like any other fault instead of burning a worker run; when the breaker alone empties the queue the tick announces once per set of hold-reason classes and stays quiet while that set is unchanged; and one idle reason composes paused, capacity, in-flight, queue, stale worker, base ref and tunnel keeper into a single answer on the CLI, of which the board serves the part its host can read and names the rest.

The graph answers what a release did to the portfolio. A release reaches the changes it made by a typed edge (the writer that exists is fixed to resolve through the field the dispatcher sets, and every existing change is backfilled — the count at capture is in the changes fixture header), each change reaches the applications it touched, and each merged change carries a dev.release record of the verdict that admitted it — so the release view, the notes and the gate's manifest list changes, applications and verdicts, and a change merged without a verdict record is named rather than invented.

Operational work this arc's own deliverables produce — defects in the selector, the reconciler, the alerts, the edges or the board pieces above — lands here rather than going unaccounted, and is held to the declared share at sprint planning. General absorption stays with R26.11/O-7; this outcome takes only defects in R26.12's deliverables. The blocking share above the one planned bead rests on this outcome.

The emergency marker is set by an operator or it is not honoured. Intake refuses the field; a writer ratchet pins the only code paths that set or clear it; a marker with no attesting operator note — or whose newest expedite note was written by a registered worker or under a model — is a hold with an alert naming the note's writer; and no dev.task may name docs/releases/** in its scope. The residual is named: the content write path records no provenance (only the note does), dev.task content is extra='allow' and the worker holds the write key (D7), so a key holder who writes both records is detected by nothing — this is detection, not prevention, until scoped tokens exist (decision record D7, 2026-09-13; no charter outcome carries that work after R26.09/O-6's re-aim); the operator predicate is interim until R26.11/O-6's identity vocabulary.

R26.13.name: The CMDB says what's next
R26.13.objective: Measured 2026-09-24/25 (live store GET-only): what enters the factory is chosen by judgement and run in arrival order. Of the 232 dev.tasks filed since 2026-09-01, 231 were outer-loop specs filed through file_task and 1 was a probe; the lane scanner has filed none of the store's 479, though it can, and its command line fails (dev.finding a862fc16). The CMDB records signals that should decide what comes next, and nothing turns them into work: 19 of 32 applications have unknown dependency posture, 13 of them in operate state; 16 EA findings are still being observed, and 36 more stay active only because the observer cannot resolve them (5c3cf2b3). The same one-page read has failed in production three times (OPS-181; OPS-191, with the EA reconciler paused since 2026-09-22; 5c3cf2b3), and more are latent. the Operator, 2026-09-24: continue the EA approach with a CMDB, make what goes into the factory next deterministic and state-driven on beads, and give work in the queue a priority so it moves through in the order planned. This arc delivers the planned order first. A release's sequence, once the Operator approves it, is recorded as precedes links, and the selector keeps it. It then stops a fourth one-page read from landing unnoticed. It then derives candidate work from CMDB state by declared rules no factory lane may edit, ranks the candidates over the dependency graph (blast radius, then age; unknown never zero), and announces the ranked list. That is Rung 0 of the actuation ladder the Operator decided on 2026-09-03, which binds every new detector: it files nothing. What it does not do, so this is chartered knowingly. Filing from the list (Rung 1) is the next arc's: it needs R26.11's planned dev.finding filer (S55-10) and a Rung 0 window that cannot elapse inside this arc. Spec writing stays with the outer loop under a gate. There are two starting rules, the 147 hand-filed findings already backlogged are not ranked, and balance stays out of every order until the Operator answers R26.12's B8b. It builds on R26.12, whose selector, served order and filing refusal must be on main first, so it opens 2026-11-16, the day after R26.12's target, and the planned order lands in sprint 58 (2026-11-16 to 11-29). It takes the precedes link that R26.12's design lists as 'Deferred and named', and nothing R26.12 rejected: no free priority number on a bead, and no release-level rank. ITSM (incident lifecycle) is deferred by the Operator's 2026-09-24 decision.

outcomes.statement: Work moves through the queue in the order it was planned. At sprint planning a release's sequence, once the Operator has approved it, is recorded as precedes links with one verb, with his approval quoted on every task. The selector ranks the planned chain as one unit and keeps its members in plan order, a held member never blocks the rest, and an expedited member still goes first on its own. The claim note and the board show 'planned position n of m'. No priority number is ever added to a bead. Lands in sprint 58.

A new one-page read cannot land unnoticed. Every implementation that reads a population of beads pages it, or is listed as a known defect with the finding that tracks its fix, or as a deliberate newest-page read with its reason. A ratchet refuses any other, proves it detects one, and drops fixed sites from the list, so the known-defect count visibly falls.

The CMDB can be read as one consistent input. A rules document, a golden file and a snapshot shape, all written by the outer loop, validate in CI. The platform builds a snapshot of the applications, services, dependency links and EA findings by paging the store, and the same tool captures the fixtures that pin its behaviour.

The platform says what could be worked on next, and why, from CMDB state alone. Declared rules derive candidates: first, an operating application whose dependencies are unknown, and an EA finding that has persisted past its declared age and is still being observed. The candidates are ranked by how many applications and services depend on the thing concerned, then by age. The ranked list is announced when it changes and printed with a one-line reason each for sprint planning. The same inputs give the same list on every host. Nothing is filed: this is Rung 0.

The factory cannot change what it is asked to derive. The rules document, the golden file that pins what each rule matches at fixed times, and the snapshot shape are refused to every factory lane at intake and by the scanner, so changing any of them needs an attended outer-loop PR, and a code change that alters a rule's meaning on the golden inputs fails its tests.

Operational work this arc's own deliverables produce (defects in the planned order, the ratchet, the snapshot, the derivation or the announcement) lands here rather than going unaccounted, and is held to the declared share at sprint planning. General absorption stays with the in_flight release that owns it.
